  phases: [{ title: 'Fix', detail: 'module, contract, workflow, docs table' }, { title: 'Recheck', detail: 'tests, live run, identity' }],
}
const WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b4'
const BASE = 'db84d76'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b4-brief.md'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b4/out'
const CACHE = '/home/user/hail-b4/cache/mesh-max'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'
const PATCH = '/home/user/hail-b4/out/final-checker/fixes.patch'
const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b4, rebased onto ${BASE}, which carries the B2 hail history; the module work sits in a WIP commit on top). Read ${BRIEF} in full first; the sections "Supervisor decisions after review (D7 to D12) and the completion list" and "Supervisor decisions after the module fix pass (D13, D14) and the completion list" are your task list: every item is applied unless already in place (check, then say so). Repository rules (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first, evidence honesty, plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names, tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package. Never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push; never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/. A python with numpy and pygrib is ${VENV}; the two cached GRIB2 files are in ${CACHE}/. Return a plain report: items applied (file and line), items already in place, items skipped with the reason, commands run with their tails.`
const FIXER = `${COMMON}\n\nYou are the completion fixer; you own website/swath.py, tests/test_swath.py, website/sources.py, website/build.py (the STORM_CONTRACTS line only), tests/test_site.py (the hail_swath expectations only), .github/workflows/website.yml (the test step line and the paths entry only) and research/globe/README.md (the GP table order only). Items: (1) apply the seven-file patch ${PATCH} (git -C ${WT} apply --check first, then git apply; the branch was rebased onto ${BASE} after the patch was written, so if a hunk no longer applies, make that hunk's change by hand to the same effect and say so). It covers B-1 (the CONTRACTS["hail_swath"] row after the storm rows in sources.py, the STORM_CONTRACTS tuple in build.py gaining "hail_swath", the key set in tests/test_site.py), B-2 (website.yml: the test step gains tests.test_swath and the paths list gains tests/test_swath.py), B-3 (a ?v= stamp on the live tile pattern, which item 3 replaces), N-2 (the GP-9 and GP-10 rows move after GP-8 in research/globe/README.md) and N-3 (the storm_levels row reads "They are never a value, never 0."). Then read the resulting CONTRACTS["hail_swath"] row against the brief (units mm shown in inches to the hundredth rounded down with exact millimetres; cadences 2 and 30 minutes; the valid time is the end of the window; -1 missing uncoloured and -3 no coverage hatched per D1; the 64-tenth floor; "an estimate, not observed hail and not damage"; the D6 thresholds; "This is not an all-clear." in the missing text): correct the row if any of these is missing. (2) D13, which is the supervisor's ruling on the checker's N-1 (D9's words win over D4's): live_files writes a tile file when the tile holds a cell at or above 64 tenths or any -3 cell (an empty cells list plus the nocov list for a tile with only -3 cells); sheet_line returns the no-coverage sentence for a -3 cell; a test on a synthetic tile that holds only -3 cells; update the tests that called this "the known gap". (3) D14: the live tile path becomes hail/live/<window>/<YYYYMMDDHHMM>/<tile>.json with the frame's valid time as the stamp (the same stamp the frame PNG's name carries); each build writes only the current stamp's folder; map_data_swath's live pattern carries the stamp folder and no ?v= query (remove the ?v= form the patch added, and its test); tests updated. (4) N-4: the "stale" entry of WORDS_SWATH in website/swath.py (about line 114) is indented eight spaces where the others use four; dedent it. (5) run ${VENV} -m unittest tests.test_swath tests.test_site tests.test_gridded tests.test_storm (tail), then the module's live path once more into ${OUT}/completion/live (list, download, decode both products; the PNG bytes; the live folder names carry the stamp; the tile count) and a sample run into ${OUT}/completion/sample (the no-coverage tiles present; count them). Report every item.`
phase('Fix')
const fixR = await agent(FIXER, { label: 'fixc:swath-completion', phase: 'Fix', model: 'haiku' })
phase('Recheck')
const recheck = await agent(`Read-only checker in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b4, rebased onto ${BASE}). Read ${BRIEF} (D1 to D14 and both completion lists). Never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/recheckc/ which you create. Run and quote: ${VENV} -m unittest discover -s tests (tail; all must pass); python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload; the module's live path now into ${OUT}/recheckc/live and your own pygrib round trip at 1,000 pixels per PNG (0 mismatches expected); the live tile folder names carry the valid-time stamp and equal the frame PNG's stamp, and no pattern carries a ?v= query; a sample run shows tile files for -3-only tiles with nocov lists and sheet_line returns the no-coverage sentence; the CONTRACTS["hail_swath"] row present and listed by STORM_CONTRACTS, so the default About page shows no hail row (measure it); a default --sample build (--now 2026-10-19T02:00:00Z) from a copy of the worktree byte-identical to the base ${BASE} build (diff -rq; the STYLE addition in gridded.py may change no default file); the YAML of website.yml parses and names tests.test_swath in the test step and tests/test_swath.py in the paths list; git -C ${WT} status --short and diff --stat ${BASE}; em-dash and banned-name counts over added lines; grep research/globe/README.md for the GP table order (GP-1 to GP-11 in order); the F1 and F2 items of the brief (the four reworded places; "never a value, never 0"; no D33 to D40 proposal label left). Write ${OUT}/b4a-recheck-completion.json with gates B4-1 to B4-5 (status, evidence), F1, F2, every completion item done or not done, and the measurements. Return that JSON as text and name every check that failed.`, { label: 'recheckc', phase: 'Recheck', model: 'haiku' })
return { fixR: (fixR || '').slice(0, 6000), recheck }
